A JJ Growth Idea for Culinary Backstreets

The Master It Can't Imagine

In 2022, Heinz typed one word — “ketchup” — into an image generator, and it kept drawing Heinz bottles. In the machine's head, ketchup is Heinz, so the AI's output became the whole ad: proof, not fake footage. This idea runs the same test on Culinary Backstreets — and lets the machine fail, on camera.

The idea in one line

Ask AI to draw “a food tour” and it hands you the tourist cliché. Then show the master it can't imagine.

How it works

Three beats. The machine goes first, the master gets the last word, and the end card does the selling.

1

The machine goes first

On screen, an AI generator is asked for “a food tour.” It produces the average of every food-tour photo ever taken: a smiling guide with a lanyard and a clipboard of “today's stops,” a posed group, a pretty market stall. Run two or three of these in a row — each one more generic than the last.

2

The cut

Hard cut to a real photograph of a real master from Culinary Backstreets' own archive: one person, one dish, decades at one stall. Named, specific, unrepeatable.

3

The line

End card: his name, his stall, his neighborhood, the date of the next walk.

The end card

The master it can't imagine.

HÜSAM HOCA  ·  WATERMELON & MELON  ·  ÜSKÜDAR, ISTANBUL  ·  NEXT WALK — [DATE]

Why it works

The AI's failure is the proof. Nothing here needs to be faked — and that's the point.

§

The AI is the evidence, not the trick

Its generic output proves the claim: the average food tour is a commodity; the master is the product.

§

It answers the reputation worry head-on

The AI half is openly AI — labeled, even bragged about. The human half is a real photograph of a real person. Nothing is faked.

§

It fits the template system

Every city gets the same structure — its own clichés, its own master, its own dish and date.

Non-negotiable

The rules

Three rules, and the idea doesn't run without all of them.

1

AI plays the tourist. It never plays the master.

2

The master is always a real photograph of a real person from CB's archive, shown with their name.

3

The AI half is labeled as AI, as big as the claim. No small print.
